title: A Proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture
summary: A guided connection between a three-page graph-theory note and display excerpts from its Lean formalization, centered on the passage from nowhere-zero flows to compatible edge pairs and cycles.
audience: Mathematically curious readers; no graph theory or Lean experience is assumed.

paper.title: A Proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture

lean.toolchain: Lean 4 (version not recorded in legacy prototype)

glossary.explanation: A closed route through a graph. In the final cover, every edge must occur in exactly two cycles, counting multiplicity.
A graph with no edge whose deletion disconnects the graph. A bridge cannot participate in the required cycle structure.
A graph in which exactly three edges meet at every vertex. The paper reduces the general problem to this case.
A conserved edge labeling in which no edge receives the zero label.
An algebraic setting where every value added to itself is zero. The proof repeatedly uses this as parity cancellation.
